G1: repoMissionIDs (migrate.go) -- the ownership signal round 2's F4
fix for ethos-6adb depends on -- read only the frozen pre-DES-058
legacy audit.jsonl file, never a SEALED chunk. `ethos audit seal` runs
at every pre-commit in an ethos-enabled repo, moving session audit
content into dated audit-<first>-<last>.jsonl chunks on essentially
every commit -- so any repo whose sessions have ever sealed (the
normal state, not an edge case) went blind, silently reopening F4's
gap. `mission migrate` shared the identical blind spot. Fixed by
reading all three sources a session's audit trail can live in: sealed
chunks (via internal/audit's exported ScanSealedDir/chunk-file
primitives), the frozen legacy file, and the live not-yet-sealed tail
-- a set union, so no dedup/ordering machinery is needed beyond what
already existed. Sealed-chunk scan errors are now soft (warn+skip,
since this feeds Create's admission control on every call and one
damaged historical chunk must not block every future create); the
legacy file and live tail keep their pre-existing stricter contract.

G2 + G3: writeContractFile's F2 fix (round 2, directory fsync after
rename) could fail AFTER the rename had already committed a correct
contract, and returned an error for it -- Create then reported
failure for a mission that existed, with a retry hitting "already
exists" and no clean path forward. Exact inverse of ethos-ouy9 (which
reported success for an ABSENT contract), no better. Decision: the
rename is the commit point. A syncDir failure past that point means
the directory-entry update's durability against a crash is
unconfirmed, not that the write failed -- dest is not "maybe wrong,"
it is right, on disk, right now. Now warned to stderr, not returned;
matches Close's existing treatment of its own post-commit trace-write
failure. Rejected: keep it an error and have Create clean up the
just-written contract -- that discards real, correct data to
manufacture retriability, and still can't distinguish "never wrote"
from "wrote then deleted to tidy up."

Fixed in `b6e48ed`, and investigating it found something worse than the finding described — including a pre-existing bug in `ethos mission migrate`.

`repoMissionIDs` wasn't *missing some* sealed audits. It was looking for a literal `audit.jsonl` **inside the sealed zone** — the pre-DES-058 legacy name (`internal/hook`'s own `sessionLegacyPath` confirms it). Real sealed chunks are named `audit-<first>-<last>.jsonl` (`internal/audit/names.go`). So for any session that had ever sealed, the function found nothing at all.

And `ethos audit seal` runs at **every pre-commit**. So this wasn't a partial blind spot — it was essentially non-functional for any actively-committed repo, which is every repo that matters. The function never got updated when DES-058 introduced the live/sealed split.

**`mission migrate` inherited it**, since it's the same function. That's a pre-existing bug this PR didn't cause, now fixed for free rather than filed and left.

The conclusion was *not* that the audit trail is the wrong foundation. It is the right signal — the implementation had simply never caught up. It now reads all three sources as a set union: sealed chunks via `internal/audit`'s exported `ScanSealedDir`, the legacy file, and the live not-yet-sealed tail. A union needs no dedup or ordering machinery.

One deliberate asymmetry: sealed-chunk read errors are soft (warn and skip) because this now runs on every `Create`; the legacy and live paths keep the stricter original contract.

Fixed in `b6e48ed`. You and Copilot found the same thing independently, and it's the exact inverse of the bug this PR set out to fix.

`ethos-ouy9` was: `Create` reports success for a contract that isn't durable. The round-2 `syncDir` fix produced: `Create` reports failure for a contract that **is** on disk — and a retry then hits "mission already exists", leaving the operator wedged with no clean path.

Decided contract: **the rename is the commit point.** A `syncDir` failure now warns to stderr and returns nil. The rationale is that the rename already committed a correct contract; erroring past that point only to have the caller delete it trades a proven-good state for a guaranteed-bad one. What's unconfirmed is the durability guarantee, not the write.

The rejected alternative — keep the error and have `Create` remove the contract it just wrote — is recorded in `DES-075` with why, rather than left as a code comment. "What happens when durability cannot be confirmed after a successful write" is precisely the question that gets re-litigated in six months otherwise.

The round-2 test was renamed to `SyncDirFailureIsWarnedNotErrored` and its assertion flipped, confirmed red against round-2 code first.

tool_input.message:
Yes, there is a round 4. Two findings, sent ~6 minutes ago and sitting in your inbox — nothing committed since b6e48ed and the tree is clean, so it has not started. Round 3 is fully done on my side: b6e48ed pushed, all three threads replied to and resolved.

Your G1 judgement was right and I want it on the record: the audit trail IS the right foundation, the implementation was just stale. Finding that it looked for a literal `audit.jsonl` — the pre-DES-058 legacy shape — inside the sealed zone, and confirming it against `internal/hook`'s own `sessionLegacyPath` rather than inferring it, turned "misses some sealed audits" into "non-functional for any repo that has ever committed". And it fixed `mission migrate`'s identical blind spot for free. That is a pre-existing bug in a shipped command, found because you read the file instead of accepting the finding's framing.

ROUND 4 — two findings, smaller than previous rounds, which is the convergence I want:

**H1 — MEDIUM. Live scan misses worktree audit files.** The new live-tail scan reads `audit.LiveSessionsDir(repoRoot)` using the Store's `repoRoot`, which resolves to the MAIN work tree. A session running in a linked worktree writes its live audit *there*, not in the main tree — so the live tail is invisible for exactly those sessions.

Not hypothetical: **every mission run today, including the two that produced this PR, executed from a linked worktree.** So the signal you just repaired remains blind to the most recent sessions — the ones whose missions are most likely to be open and un-migrated.

The asymmetry that makes it subtle: SEALED chunks live under the main tree because they travel with commits, so your G1 fix is correct for those. Only the LIVE, not-yet-sealed tail is per-checkout. Mechanism is your call — enumerate live dirs across the main tree plus linked worktrees, or resolve the live path per-checkout — but put the decision in DES-075, because "where does live audit live relative to the store root" is now the THIRD distinct bug this repo has had on that exact question (ethos-vqwn, ethos-5yej, this).

**H2 — cosmetic but real.** `repoMissionIDs` emits warnings prefixed `"ethos: mission migrate"`, but it now runs inside `Store.conflictScanIDs` during `mission create` admission control. An operator running `create` sees a migrate warning and reasonably concludes a migration is underway. Prefix should name the actual caller or be neutral.

Small, but the same class as `ethos-lldo` — the first bug in this entire triage — where a message described a code path that was no longer taken and pointed the reader away from the real problem. A warning naming the wrong command does that to someone debugging at 2am.

Regression red first for H1. `make check` per commit, detached gate with both counts, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` still 0.
